title: Provisioning orchestrator retry/backoff policy + quarantine triggers
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
linked_artifacts: Confluence: ADR-017 Provision-to-ready readiness state machine
description:
Context
- As we move Dedicated capacity bring-up to an automated provision-to-ready workflow, the orchestrator needs a consistent retry/backoff policy per step, and clear quarantine criteria.
- Today, manual “just retry it” and unbounded retries cause (a) long tail time-to-ready, (b) noisy metrics/alerts, and (c) thrash on flaky validations (notably NCCL smoke + network jitter).

Goals
- Bound retries and time spent per node/step while keeping success rate high on transient failures.
- Make retry behavior predictable and observable (attempt counters, last error, next retry time, step duration).
- Define when to quarantine vs. keep retrying vs. reimage.
- Ensure policy aligns with SRE alerting expectations (avoid paging loops during staged rollout).

Non-goals
- Redesign of scheduler/autoscaler behavior.
- Comprehensive “self-heal everything” framework; this is focused on initial bring-up and readiness validation.

Definitions
- Attempt: a single execution of a provisioning/validation step.
- Retryable: failure class where a subsequent attempt is likely to succeed without operator intervention (e.g., temporary API errors, transient network failures).
- Non-retryable (fatal): failure class that should stop the workflow and either quarantine or require operator action (e.g., GPU health hard failures).
- Quarantine: node is removed from eligibility for serving pools and surfaced to operators with a reason + artifact pointers; re-entry requires explicit operator action (reimage / override) or a later automated “revalidate after reimage” path.

Proposed policy (approved)

A) Global orchestrator defaults
- Backoff algorithm: exponential backoff with full jitter.
  - base_delay: 30s
  - multiplier: 2.0
  - max_delay: 15m
  - jitter: full (random in [0, backoff])
- Default max_attempts_per_step: 3
- Default step_deadline: 30m (hard stop; if exceeded -> quarantine with reason=STEP_TIMEOUT)
- Default total_workflow_deadline: 2h from Allocated -> Ready (if exceeded -> quarantine with reason=WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT)
- Retry budget guardrail:
  - If 3 consecutive steps fail due to the same root cause class (e.g., NETWORK_UNREACHABLE), quarantine early to avoid thrash.

B) Step-by-step retry/timeout/quarantine table

1) Bootstrap / agent heartbeat (node-online)
- What it is: wait for node agent to heartbeat + basic node identity (instance_id, image_version, gpu_sku).
- Retryable failures: missing heartbeat.
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 6
  - base_delay: 20s, max_delay: 5m
  - step_deadline: 20m
- Quarantine:
  - If no heartbeat by deadline -> quarantine (BOOTSTRAP_NO_HEARTBEAT).

2) Kube join (node-joined)
- Retryable failures: kubelet registration transient failures, API throttling, short-lived auth token issues.
- Non-retryable: repeated TLS/cert misconfig, node name collisions, obvious config drift vs baseline (kubelet flags mismatch).
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 4
  - base_delay: 30s, max_delay: 10m
  - step_deadline: 25m
- Quarantine:
  - Quarantine after max_attempts with KUBE_JOIN_FAILED + include last 50 lines of kubelet journal pointer.
  - Immediate quarantine if config drift detected (KUBELET_CONFIG_BASELINE_MISMATCH) (this should be “reimage required”).

3) Preflight: GPU discovery + driver/toolkit parity
- Retryable: nvidia-smi transient failure due to driver init on first boot.
- Non-retryable: driver version mismatch vs pinned image channel, missing devices, persistent NVML errors.
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 3
  - base_delay: 1m, max_delay: 10m
  - step_deadline: 20m
- Quarantine triggers (immediate):
  - GPU not enumerated after attempt 2 (GPU_NOT_FOUND)
  - Driver mismatch (DRIVER_PARITY_FAILED)
  - NVML init error persists across 2 attempts (NVML_INIT_FAILED)

4) Networking + storage sanity (baseline checks)
- Retryable: packet loss spikes, transient DNS issues, temporary EBS attachment lag.
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 5
  - base_delay: 30s, max_delay: 10m
  - step_deadline: 30m
- Quarantine:
  - Only after step_deadline, unless we detect a known-fatal signature (e.g., no NIC, persistent route missing) -> quarantine (NETWORK_CONFIG_INVALID).

5) Postflight: NCCL smoke test
- Known risk: flake rate due to transient fabric issues, noisy neighbors, early-boot contention.
- Retryable: NCCL timeout, “connection reset” style errors.
- Non-retryable: consistent topology mismatch, consistent bandwidth far below floor across attempts.
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 3
  - base_delay: 5m, max_delay: 20m (cooldown is intentional to avoid hammering fabric during transient issues)
  - step_deadline: 60m
  - Per-attempt timeout: 10m
- Quarantine:
  - Quarantine on 3rd failure with NCCL_SMOKE_FAILED.
  - Immediate quarantine if NCCL reports topology/peer mapping errors that indicate miswired fabric (NCCL_TOPOLOGY_ERROR).

6) Postflight: inference perf canary (lightweight)
- Policy:
  - max_attempts: 2
  - base_delay: 2m, max_delay: 10m
  - step_deadline: 30m
- Quarantine:
  - Quarantine after 2 failures with PERF_CANARY_FAILED.

C) When to reimage vs quarantine
- Orchestrator default action is quarantine (not infinite reimage loops).
- Operator-driven remediation:
  - For baseline drift / driver mismatch / kubelet config mismatch: recommended action is “reimage to stable channel”, then re-run validations.
  - For transient network/storage flakes: safe action is “retry validations” once; if repeat -> quarantine.
- Future (not in scope): automated single reimage attempt for a narrow set of image-related failures (guarded by a feature flag), with a strict cap of 1 reimage per instance_id.

D) Observability requirements (must be emitted)
- Per step:
  - attempt_count (counter)
  - step_duration_seconds (histogram)
  - backoff_seconds (histogram)
  - error_class (enum label; low-cardinality)
- Workflow:
  - time_to_ready_seconds (histogram)
  - quarantine_count (counter) labeled by reason + gpu_sku + region
- Cardinality constraints (SRE requirement):
  - NO per-node-id tags on metrics.
  - Node identifiers only in logs/traces with sampling.

E) State machine integration
- Orchestrator writes transition reasons into readiness service:
  - last_failed_step
  - last_error_class
  - last_error_summary (short, sanitized)
  - validation_artifacts_uri (pointer)
  - next_retry_at (timestamp)
- Quarantine is a terminal state from the orchestrator’s perspective.

Acceptance criteria
- Policy documented and reviewed by SRE.
- Implemented configuration is parameterized (per step overrides) and behind rollout flag.
- Control plane surfaces: attempt_count, last_failed_step, last_error_class, next_retry_at.
- No infinite retries observed in staged rollout; overall workflow deadline enforced.

SRE review notes (captured + addressed)
- (Sean Gallagher) Ensure we don’t page on expected early-rollout flake spikes; retry policy must prevent “retry storms.”
  - Addressed by: longer cooldown for NCCL; bounded retries; workflow deadline; metrics without node-level tags.
- (Miles Thornton) Backoff must be jittered; otherwise synchronized retries can amplify fabric/API issues.
  - Addressed by: full-jitter exponential backoff.
- (Aisha Bello) Quarantine reasons must be low-cardinality enums; free-form strings in metrics are a no-go.
  - Addressed by: enumerated error_class/quarantine_reason; keep verbose detail in logs/artifact bundle.

Rollout plan (for this policy)
- Start enabled for us-east / A100 only (feature flag), with alerting in “ticket-only” mode for 48h.
- Promote to paging alerts only after:
  - quarantine rate < 2% sustained
  - NCCL flake < 1% sustained OR understood/mitigated

Notes / follow-ups
- If NCCL flake remains >1% after cooldown tuning, consider splitting NCCL into:
  - quick “connectivity” check (fast fail)
  - slower bandwidth floor check (run only after node otherwise healthy)
- Add explicit “operator override: mark ready” path only for non-production pools (do not allow on Dedicated serving pools).
comments: 2025-10-06 (Rafael Mendes): Please add a hard workflow deadline. Otherwise we’ll accumulate stuck nodes in Provisioning/Validating and it’ll inflate time-to-ready without triggering quarantine. Also +1 to full jitter on exponential backoff.

2025-10-07 (Miles Thornton): Strong preference for error classes as enums. We’ve been burned by high-cardinality labels when people include raw error strings. Also ensure backoff and attempt counters are visible in readiness service so oncall doesn’t need to grep logs.

2025-10-09 (Aisha Bello): For NCCL smoke retries, do a longer cooldown than other steps; immediate retries tend to keep failing when fabric is congested. Also please confirm we won’t tag metrics with node IDs.
2025-10-10 (Gabe Wilson): Added step-by-step table + workflow deadline. Implemented full-jitter backoff in orchestrator library; plumbed error_class/quarantine_reason enums into readiness writes.

2025-10-16 (Sean Gallagher): Looks good. Only remaining concern is retry storms during rollout; please ensure the default base_delay isn’t too low for kube join when API is throttling. Suggest 30s base with max 10m and cap attempts at 4.
2025-10-18 (Vanessa Ortiz): Updated kube join base_delay to 30s and confirmed attempt cap. Marking done; implementation tracked in follow-on PRs.
